kernels.name: qualifying_child_residence_gate
kernels.query_clause: Whether the individual is the taxpayer's qualifying child under §152(c)(1), limited to failure of the mandatory shared-principal-abode duration condition in §152(c)(1)(B).
kernels.source_quote: (B) who has the same principal place of abode as the taxpayer for more than one-half of such taxable year,

value.rationale: The agricultural kernel implements only §3306(a)(2)(A), not the alternative day-and-worker test. It keeps separate totals for the query year and preceding calendar year and requires either total independently to reach $20,000. Only amounts explicitly given as wages for stated agricultural labor are counted; it does not create another wage test. A period crossing calendar years is unresolved because its amount cannot be allocated or duplicated. A known threshold witness yields Entailment despite unrelated unresolved records. Contradiction is available only when the finite native record was successfully extracted, no relevant allocation remains unresolved, and neither year's separate total reaches the threshold; no separate exhaustive-history assertion is required under the supplied finite-case semantics. The residence kernel treats the query year as the taxable-year period specified by the task, clips and unions inclusive joint-residence intervals containing both queried persons, and applies the strict more-than-one-half requirement. A successfully extracted finite record can establish Contradiction when the observed joint-residence union is no more than half the year; failed or ambiguous extraction remains unhandled. No address or separate principal-abode assertion is required because each persons array denotes people sharing the same home during that interval. Passing this gate remains unhandled and does not establish relationship, age, return status, or the complete §152(c)(1) claim. The supplied source states no exception to its residence-duration requirement.
